name: Solidgate Card Payments for WooCommerce
author: Solidgate

sections.description:
Solidgate Card Payments for WooCommerce embeds the Solidgate payment form directly inside your WooCommerce checkout page. Customers fill in their card details inline and click Place Order — no redirect, no modal, no leaving your site.

Key features

  • Inline card form — Solidgate card fields render inside the WooCommerce payment section as soon as the customer selects this gateway.
  • Custom submission — card processing is triggered by WooCommerce’s own Place Order button, not a separate Solidgate button. Keeps the native checkout UX intact.
  • Auto-initialization — the form loads immediately on page load when the gateway is pre-selected, and re-initializes automatically after coupon or shipping changes.
  • Billing email pre-fill — when the customer fills in their email, the form re-initializes with it so Solidgate can suppress its own email field.
  • Webhook-based order updates — order status (approved, declined, refunded) is updated in real time via Solidgate webhooks.
  • Refunds from WooCommerce admin — issue full or partial refunds directly from the order screen.
  • HPOS compatible — fully supports WooCommerce High-Performance Order Storage (custom order tables).
  • Logging — optional debug logging to the WooCommerce log for troubleshooting.

Third-Party Service

This plugin connects to the Solidgate payment platform (https://solidgate.com) to process payments. Solidgate is a third-party service — by using this plugin you are subject to their terms and privacy policy.

What data is sent to Solidgate:

  • Order details: amount, currency, order ID
  • Customer billing country and email address (used for payment form pre-fill)
  • Payment method data entered by the customer inside the Solidgate-hosted iframe (card numbers are never processed by your server)
  • Webhook signatures sent from Solidgate to your site to confirm payment status

When data is sent: Data is transmitted at checkout when the customer initiates payment, and via webhooks when Solidgate sends order status updates (approved, declined, refunded).

  • Solidgate Terms of Service: https://solidgate.com/terms/
  • Solidgate Privacy Policy: https://solidgate.com/privacy-policy/

External services used

  • https://cdn.solidgate.com — Solidgate JavaScript SDK loaded on the checkout page to render the card form.
  • https://form-v2.solidgate.com — Solidgate-hosted iframe that renders card input fields. Card data is entered and processed entirely within this iframe; your server never handles raw card numbers.
  • Solidgate API — your server calls the Solidgate API to create a signed payment session and to process refunds.

Requirements

  • WordPress 5.6 or later
  • WooCommerce 7.0 or later
  • PHP 7.4 or later
  • A Solidgate merchant account — sign up at solidgate.com
sections.installation:
1. Upload the solidgate-card-payments folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install via Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin in WordPress admin.
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen.
  3. Go to WooCommerce > Settings > Payments and click Set up next to “Solidgate Card Payments”.
  4. Enter your credentials from the Solidgate merchant dashboard:
    • Public Key
    • Private Key
    • Webhook Public Key
    • Webhook Private Key
  5. Set the gateway title (shown to customers at checkout) and save.
  6. In the Solidgate dashboard, set your webhook URL to:
    • https://yoursite.com/wp-json/sgcp/v1/webhook
sections.faq:
Where do I get my API keys?

Log in to your Solidgate merchant dashboard and navigate to Settings > API Keys.

Is the plugin PCI compliant?

Yes. Card data is entered directly inside a Solidgate-hosted iframe served from form-v2.solidgate.com. Your server never handles raw card numbers — only a signed session token is exchanged.

What currencies are supported?

All currencies enabled on your Solidgate merchant account.

How do I set up the webhook?

In your Solidgate merchant dashboard, add a webhook endpoint pointing to https://yoursite.com/wp-json/sgcp/v1/webhook. Solidgate will send order status events (approved, declined, refunded) to this URL, and the plugin will update the corresponding WooCommerce order automatically.

Does the plugin support refunds?

Yes. You can issue full or partial refunds directly from the WooCommerce order screen (WooCommerce > Orders > [order] > Refund). The plugin calls the Solidgate refund API automatically.

Is the plugin compatible with WooCommerce HPOS?

Yes. The plugin declares compatibility with WooCommerce High-Performance Order Storage (custom order tables) and uses wc_get_orders() for all order lookups.

What happens if the payment form fails to load?

The container shows an error message prompting the customer to refresh the page. The form also automatically re-attempts initialization after WooCommerce recalculates checkout totals.
sections.changelog:
1.0.17

  • Fixed: order_description is now built from WooCommerce cart item names instead of a generic label, making it meaningful in the Solidgate dashboard.
  • Fixed: All string fields are truncated to their API maximum before submission (order_description → 255 chars, order_id → 255 chars, customer_email → 100 chars) to prevent error 2.01 length validation failures.

1.0.16

  • Fixed: Text domain changed to match plugin slug (solidgate-card-payments-for-woocommerce) — required for WP.org translation compatibility.
  • Added: Requires Plugins: woocommerce header (WordPress 6.5+) for formal WooCommerce dependency declaration.
  • Updated: Solidgate PHP SDK vendor source updated to v1.6.2 (FormInitDTO, FormUpdateDTO, FormResignDTO DTOs; backward-compatible interface).
  • Updated: composer.json now requires guzzlehttp/guzzle ^7.13 (was ^7.0) to track current stable security releases.

1.0.15

  • Improved: Thank-you page status check is now non-blocking. Instead of calling the Solidgate status API synchronously during page render, a lightweight JS script polls a new /sgcp/v1/poll-status REST endpoint in the background and reloads the page once the payment is confirmed — thank-you page now loads instantly.
  • Added: 8 s timeout (5 s connect) on all Solidgate status API calls (card and APM) to prevent slow API responses from holding PHP workers.
  • Fixed: Removed dead handle_webhook() method left over from the ?wc-api= removal in 1.0.13.

1.0.14

  • Added: Solidgate status check on the WooCommerce thank-you page. When the customer lands on the order confirmation screen and the order is still on-hold, the plugin calls pay.solidgate.com/api/v1/status with the Solidgate order ID and immediately completes the order if the payment is confirmed — bridging the gap between checkout redirect and webhook delivery.

1.0.13

  • Changed: Removed legacy ?wc-api= webhook handler and the hourly cron job. Webhook delivery is handled exclusively via /wp-json/sgcp/v1/webhook. Missed webhooks can be recovered manually using the “Check Solidgate payment status” order action added in 1.0.12.

1.0.12

  • Added: Solidgate status API integration for stuck order recovery. A “Check Solidgate payment status” action is now available on the WC order edit screen, and an hourly cron automatically checks on-hold orders from the last 24 hours and updates them if the payment was approved, failed, or refunded. Supports both card and APM orders.

1.0.11

  • Fixed: Webhook HPOS recovery no longer depends on wp_postmeta. In full-HPOS mode (no legacy compatibility sync), wp_postmeta is never written — the missing wc_orders row is now inserted directly using the order ID extracted from the HPOS exception, falling back to wc-on-hold status when the post status is unavailable.

1.0.10

  • Fixed: Webhook handler now recovers from the case where wc_orders has no row at all for a given order (orphaned HPOS meta — wc_orders_meta entry exists but the parent wc_orders row is missing). The handler falls back to wp_postmeta, inserts the missing row, and retries. Covers both broken-HPOS scenarios: NULL type column (1.0.9) and missing row entirely (1.0.10).

1.0.9

  • Fixed: Webhook handler now recovers from WooCommerce HPOS “Could not find classname” errors when the wc_orders.type column is NULL or unregistered — patches it to shop_order and retries.

1.0.8

  • Fixed: Webhook handler now recovers from WooCommerce HPOS “Could not find classname” errors — first attempt via direct wc_get_order($id) fallback.
  • Added: Success log entry after payment_complete() for easier debugging (“Webhook: order N marked complete”).

1.0.7

  • Fixed: Orders staying “on-hold” after successful payment due to a webhook/checkout race condition. The Solidgate webhook (server-to-server) typically arrives before the customer’s browser re-submits the WooCommerce checkout form and process_payment() stores the order meta. The webhook handler now returns 404 when the order is not found yet, triggering a Solidgate retry — by which time the meta is already stored and the order updates correctly.

1.0.6

  • Fixed: Webhook handler now recognizes settle_ok and settled statuses from Solidgate (sent after immediate capture with settle_interval: 0). Orders were staying in “on-hold” after successful payment because only approved was handled.
  • Fixed: Added auth_ok webhook handling — stores Solidgate order ID and adds an order note when authorization is received, so the primary order lookup is always populated before the capture callback arrives.
  • Fixed: _sgcp_solidgate_order_id meta is now stored in process_payment() alongside _sgcp_order_token, eliminating a race condition where the webhook primary lookup failed if the callback fired before any prior meta update.
  • Fixed: Idempotency — duplicate webhook events (Solidgate retries) are now deduplicated via solidgate-event-id header; processed IDs are stored for one week per Solidgate documentation.
  • Fixed: Status regression guard — a late declined webhook cannot flip an already-processing or completed order to failed (Solidgate webhooks are not guaranteed to arrive in order).

1.0.5

  • Fixed: Webhook endpoint migrated from ?wc-api=sgcp_webhook to /wp-json/sgcp/v1/webhook for reliable delivery across all hosting environments.

1.0.4

  • Added: Card form initializes once; subsequent email or total changes use form.update() (new /sgcp/v1/update endpoint) instead of re-creating the payment session.
  • Fixed: Switching payment method radio buttons no longer re-initializes the form — SDK instance stays alive and is reused on return.
  • Fixed: Removed redundant show()/hide() on the form container; WooCommerce’s own payment box animation is used exclusively, eliminating overlap between payment methods.
  • Fixed: Scroll-anchor jump when the payment box appears or disappears (overflow-anchor: none on #payment).
  • Added: Skeleton loader with shimmer animation shown while the Solidgate iframe loads, followed by a smooth fade-in on ready.

1.0.3

  • Fixed: Plugin URI updated to plugin-specific page to resolve plugin/author URI mismatch warning.
  • Added: Customer IP address passed to Solidgate init payload (ip_address); resolved from X-Forwarded-For, HTTP_CLIENT_IP, or REMOTE_ADDR, public IPs only.

1.0.2

  • Fixed: CVV tooltip hidden via Solidgate SDK styles API to prevent clipping inside the iframe.
  • Fixed: Payment form now initializes immediately on page load when the gateway is pre-selected.
  • Fixed: Form re-initializes when billing email is filled in, so Solidgate receives customer_email and can suppress its own email field.
  • Fixed: Removed payment_intent from init payload (not a valid Solidgate parameter).
  • Added: settle_interval: 0 added to payment init payload.
  • Added: geo_country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-3) embedded in order_id for traceability.
  • Changed: overflow: visible on payment box wrapper to prevent parent-level tooltip clipping.

1.0.1

  • Fixed: Stable tag and Tested up to values corrected in readme.txt.
  • Fixed: SDK script version set to prevent browser caching issues.
  • Fixed: Webhook order lookup migrated to meta_query array format.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
